Academy Foundations: how to read a medicine Most harm done to animals with medicine in India is not done by the wrong drug. It is done by the right drug in the wrong strength, by the wrong route, for the wrong species, or from a bottle that spent a summer in a car. This module gives you the vocabulary to avoid all four. Tell a brand name from the molecule inside it and read a strength off any label. Decode a prescription line, including the abbreviations vets use. Say why a cat, a dog, a cow and a horse each need a different rule book. Store vaccines and medicines so that they still work when needed. 1.1 What is actually in the box: brand, molecule and strength Every medicine has one true name, the generic or molecule name, and any number of brand names. The molecule is what acts; the brand is what the shop stocks. Do this Do this Before giving anything, read three things aloud: the molecule, the strength per tablet or per mL, and the weight of the animal. If any of the three is missing, stop and ask. Meloxicam is meloxicam whether the carton says Melonex, Metacam or a chemist's own brand. The dangerous variable is not the brand but the strength : how many milligrams of the molecule sit in one tablet or one millilitre. Human meloxicam tablets are 7.5 mg and 15 mg. The veterinary oral suspension for dogs is 1.5 mg per mL, and the injection is usually 5 mg per mL. A 5 kg dog on a correct 0.1 mg per kg dose needs 0.5 mg. One human 7.5 mg tablet is fifteen times that. The same is true of the antibiotic amoxicillin-clavulanate, which comes as 375 mg and 625 mg human tablets, veterinary 250 mg and 500 mg tablets, and paediatric syrups of several strengths. Reading "give one tablet" without reading which tablet is how overdoses happen. Basis Merck Vet Manual Plumb's 1.2 Reading an Indian label: Rx, Schedule H, H1, expiry, withdrawal Indian labels carry a small set of legally fixed phrases. Once you can read them, a strip of tablets tells you how it may be bought, how long it lasts and, for a farm animal, how long its milk or meat must be discarded. Warning 6 facts Careful A strip with the Schedule H warning that a shop hands over without a prescription is a shop breaking the law, not a sign the drug is safe to use casually. The warning is on the strip because of what the drug can do. "Schedule H drug. Warning: To be sold by retail on the prescription of a Registered Medical Practitioner only." Prescription only. Most antibiotics, NSAIDs, steroids and sedatives carry it. The definition of a registered practitioner in the Drugs Rules includes a person engaged in the practice of veterinary medicine, which is why a vet's prescription is enough at a chemist. Schedule H1 , a stricter class introduced in 2014, covers third and fourth generation cephalosporins, carbapenems, anti-tuberculosis drugs and a number of habit-forming drugs. The chemist must record the prescriber, the patient and the drug in a register kept for three years. If a vet prescribes one, expect the pharmacist to ask for the prescription and write it down. "For veterinary use only" or "For animal treatment only" marks a veterinary licence. It does not make the drug gentler; it means the strength and label were set for animals. Mfg., Exp., Batch No. Expiry is the last day the manufacturer guarantees potency under the stated storage. A vaccine or an antibiotic past expiry is not a bargain, it is a coin toss. Withdrawal period on livestock medicines: the number of days after the last dose during which milk must not be sold and the animal must not be slaughtered for food. FSSAI sets residue limits for antibiotics in food; the withdrawal period is how a farmer stays under them. Storage "Store below 25 °C", "Store at 2 °C to 8 °C, do not freeze", "Protect from light". In an Indian May, "below 25 °C" means a refrigerator or an air-conditioned room, not a shelf. Basis Drugs Rules 1945 FSSAI 1.3 Reading a prescription line, and the abbreviations vets use A complete prescription line answers seven questions: which animal, what weight, which molecule, what strength, how much, by which route, how often and for how long. If one is missing, the line is not complete. Table An example, as it might be written for a 12 kg community dog with tick fever: Doxycycline 100 mg tab, 1/2 tab PO BID x 28 days, with food. Read it as: doxycycline, 100 mg tablets, half a tablet, by mouth, twice a day, for twenty-eight days, given with food. Half of 100 mg is 50 mg, which for 12 kg is about 4.2 mg per kg twice daily, inside the published range of 5 mg per kg twice a day or 10 mg per kg once a day. The arithmetic is checkable, which is the point of writing it out. The abbreviations are Latin shorthand and every vet in India uses them: Written Means Written Means PO by mouth OD or SID once a day SC or S/C under the skin BID twice a day, 12 hours apart IM into muscle TID three times a day, 8 hours apart IV into a vein QID four times a day q8h, q12h, q24h every 8, 12, 24 hours EOD every other day prn as needed, within a stated limit stat at once, one dose now tab, cap tablet, capsule susp, syr suspension (shake), syrup mg/kg milligrams per kilogram of body weight mL millilitre, the volume of a liquid Dose is the amount given at one time. Dosage is the whole plan: dose, route, interval and duration. When a vet says "the dosage is 5 mg per kg BID for 28 days", each of those four parts is a separate instruction, and each one matters. Basis Plumb's Merck Vet Manual 1.4 Routes: why the same drug is a different drug by mouth, under the skin and in a vein The route decides how fast a medicine arrives, how much of it arrives, and what it can damage on the way. Changing the route changes the dose, so a route is never a detail to improvise. Warning 6 facts Careful Never give an injectable by mouth or an oral liquid by injection, never inject anything into a vein yourself, and never put anything into the mouth of an animal that is unconscious, fitting or vomiting: it goes into the lungs. By mouth (PO) slowest, safest for a layperson, and the only route a caregiver should ordinarily use. Some drugs are destroyed in the stomach or the rumen, which is why a cow's oral dose can differ so much from a dog's. U

pages.body: Policies and achievements | People for Animals Every drive, camp and open day is free to attend ✕ Our work Policies and achievements. Thirty years · eight fronts What changed. Drag or swipe to turn · choose a card to open it 0 fronts worked at once 0 decades of it, from 1994 Everything Courts & law Farmed animals Policy & systems Wildlife & shows Community dogs Testing & labs Teaching Working animals 001 Helped end cosmetic testing on animals in India PFA’s campaign contributed to India becoming one of the first countries in the world to prohibit cosmetic testing on animals (2014) and to ban the import of animal-tested cosmetics. Courts & law 2014 002 Secured a ban on the export of shark fins Advocated for an end to shark-fin exports, and in 2015 the Government prohibited the export of shark fins of all species, a ban subsequently upheld in court. Wildlife & shows 2015 003 Protected Rajasthan's camels Campaigned for the camel's recognition as Rajasthan's State Animal and for the 2015 State law prohibiting camel slaughter and regulating their movement and export. Farmed animals 2015 004 Advocated for the ban on animal dissection in schools PFA’s legal and policy action led the Government of India to ban dissection for school students, implemented in 1998. Testing & labs 1998 005 Shaped India's community-dog (ABC) framework Assisted the Government of India to develop the Animal Birth Control Rules of 2001 and 2023, and have supported States and municipalities to implement scientific sterilisation and anti-rabies programmes. Courts & law 2001 006 Delivered frontline veterinary care on the Char Dham route Transformed equine welfare on the Kedarnath Yatra. Since 2024 PFA has delivered veterinary care, health screening and rescue for working equines, by operating an equine infirmary at Rudraprayag. PFA’s advocacy led the Uttarakhand High Court to direct mandatory registration, rest periods, a ban on operations between sunset and sunrise, and mandatory health check of animals before deployment. Courts & law 2024 007 Put animals into India's disaster response After leading the rescue of more than 6,000 animals in the 2013 Uttarakhand floods, PFA assisted the National Disaster Management Authority to develop Animal-Inclusive Disaster Risk Reduction guidelines. Policy & systems 2013 008 Drove reform of laboratory-animal use PFA’s sustained campaign contributed to major reforms in India's laboratory-animal regulation and earned international recognition through the Lush Prize. Testing & labs 009 Pushed States to build real animal-welfare institutions Campaigned nationwide for functional State Animal Welfare Boards, working with every State on the long-pending directive and moving the Supreme Court to require their establishment. Courts & law 010 Helped consumers make informed choices Assisted the Government of India to introduce the mandatory vegetarian and non-vegetarian symbols (red and green dots) on packaged food products. Policy & systems 011 Stopped the illegal cross-border animal-sacrifice trade at Gadhimai In Gauri Maulekhi v. Union of India, PFA moved the Supreme Court, which in 2014 directed authorities to halt the illegal transport of animals across the India-Nepal border for mass sacrifice, establishing a lasting precedent for protecting animals trafficked across international borders. With the Government of Bihar, PFA prevented the trafficking and ritual slaughter of about 700 animals ahead of Nepal's Gadhimai festival, working with the Sashastra Seema Bal from Motihari (30 November-9 December 2024) to intercept smuggling and provide emergency veterinary care. Courts & law 2014 012 Dog Breeding and Marketing Rules, 2017 Obtained directions from the Hon’ble Delhi High Court and assisted the Government of India to develop the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Dog Breeding and Marketing) Rules, 2017, creating a national framework for commercial dog breeding and sale. Courts & law 2017 013 Regulation of Livestock Markets Rules, 2017 Obtained directions from the Hon’ble Supreme Court and assisted the Government of India to develop the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Regulation of Livestock Markets) Rules, 2017, introducing welfare safeguards for the handling and sale of animals at livestock markets. Courts & law 2017 014 Care and Maintenance of Case Property Animals Rules, 2017 After securing directions from the Hon’ble Supreme Court, PFA assisted the Government of India to develop the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Care and Maintenance of Case Property Animals) Rules, 2017, protecting animals seized in cruelty cases during the pendency of proceedings. Courts & law 2017 015 Pet Shop Rules, 2018 Obtained directions from the Hon’ble Delhi High Court and assisted the Government of India to develop the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Pet Shop) Rules, 2018, mandating registration and welfare standards for pet shops. Courts & law 2018 016 Environmental rules for dairy farms and gaushalas Advocated, through proceedings before the National Green Tribunal, for stronger environmental regulation of dairy farms and gaushalas, contributing to the Central Pollution Control Board's Guidelines for Environmental Management of Dairy Farms and Gaushalas (2020, revised 2021). Courts & law 2020 017 Environmental rules for poultry farms Advocated, before the National Green Tribunal, for stronger environmental regulation of poultry farms, contributing to the Central Pollution Control Board's Guidelines for Environmental Management of Poultry Farms. Courts & law 018 The Package of Practice for Organised Pig Farms Co-authored the Package of Practice for Organised Pig Farms, with the National Research Center on Pig, Guwahati. This serves as an SOP which promotes welfare of lakhs of pigs and scientific management practices to prevent cruelty. Farmed animals 019 Conditions improved for 10,000 pigs across 53 farms Documented welfare violations at 53 pig farms and secured regulatory directions improving conditions for more than 10,000 pigs in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana. Farmed animals 020 Confinement crates taken off IndiaMART Facilitated the removal of approximately 1,000 confinement-crate listings from IndiaMART, curbing the sale of equipment used for intensive pig confinement. Farmed animals 021 A scientific pig housing unit at Rishikesh Established, with the Government of Uttarakhand and ICAR-NRCP, a Scientific Pig Housing Model Demonstration Unit in Rishikesh, and PFA train veterinary officers in humane, welfare-oriented pig farming. Farmed animals 022 31,000 poultry farmers reached across six States Conducted more than 150 farm visits and 10 training programmes, reaching over 31,000 poultry farmers across six States with guidance on cage-free production. Farmed animals 023 A cage-free poultry training facility in Tamil Nadu Established a cage-free poultry demonstration and training facility in Tamil Nadu, and are developing a model cage-free farm and training centre with the Government of Uttar Pradesh and ICAR-CARI. Farmed animals 024 Twenty-five companies moved on cage-free eggs Engaged more than 25 Indian and international companies on cage-free egg sourcing and brought farmers, retailers and institutional buyers together to grow cage-free supply. Farmed animals 025 Illegal dairies off the Yamuna floodplains Litigated before the National Green Tribunal against illegally operated dairies polluting the Yamuna floodplains, causing illegal dairy operations and unauthorised colonies to be removed. Courts & law 026 Sixteen hundred vials of spurious oxytocin seized PFA’s intervention against the illegal use of spurious oxytocin in dairies contributed to enforcement action, including the seizure of around 1,600 vials, closure of illegal facilities and arrests. Policy & systems 027 Science partnerships with ICAR and veterinary universities Work with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (including ICAR-CARI, ICAR-NRCP and ICAR-CIFA) and veterinary universities to promote science-based, higher-welfare husbandry across poultry, pig and fish farming. Farmed animals 028 The only equine infirmary at Rudraprayag Manage the only equine infirmary at Rudraprayag in collaboration with the District Administration; the Uttarakhand High Court has recognised its role in caring for equines on the Kedarnath route. Government records placed before the Uttarakhand High Court recorded more than 21,000 equines screened and 3,482 treatments; its programme records report over 700 unfit equines kept off the track on medical grounds. Courts & law 029 Happy Home Sanctuary, no tie and no cage Operate Happy Home Sanctuary at Chharba, Dehradun on a no-tie, no-cage model, currently caring for around 300 rescued animals, including working equines. Working animals 030 Phasewise ABC programmes in two States Assisted the Governments of Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh to develop phasewise ABC programs with robust infrastructure, monitoring and budgetary allocation. Community dogs 031 The country’s only approved ABC training centre Assisted the Government of Uttar Pradesh in developing the country’s only Government approved training center in Lucknow. Teaching 032 Seats on State ABC monitoring committees Serve on ABC Monitoring Committees and advisory mechanisms in several States to support effective implementation. Community dogs 033 Campaigned against the illegal wildlife trade at the Sonepur (Sonpur) fair in Bihar Secured court directions to ban the sale of all wildlife at the fair. Wildlife & shows 034 Mobile zoos prohibited A 1995 intervention against mini and mobile zoos contributed to the prohibition of mobile zoos and stronger regulation of animal exhibition and transport, and PFA assisted in closing illegal facilities and rescuing animals. Wildlife & shows 1995 035 Bull-fighting banned in Goa Secured Bombay High Court directions in 1996 banning bull-fighting and other animal fights in Goa under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act. Courts & law 1996 036 Film safeguards extended to shoots abroad Advocated for India's animal-welfare safeguards to apply to Indian films using animals in sequences shot abroad, closing a loophole under the Performing Animals (Registration) Rules, 2001. Courts & law 2001 037 Animals in film and television, monitored Monitor the use of animals in films and television and take legal action against productions involving animal abuse. Wildlife & shows 038 Circuses regulated and wild animals rescued Worked with central and State authorities to regulate circuses and enforce the ban on prohibited wild animals, helping secure the rescue and rehabilitation of circus animals. Wildlife & shows 039 Wild animals prohibited as performers Campaigned for the prohibition on using wild animals such as bears, tigers, lions, monkeys and panthers as performing animals. Wildlife & shows 040 Camels taken off Mumbai’s beaches A 1994 petition removed camels from beach rides in Mumbai and returned them to their native habitat. Courts & law 1994 041 The whipping of racehorses regulated Campaigned against the whipping of racehorses, leading to regulation on racecourses, with its representatives serving as welfare checkers at turf clubs. About the role People For Animals is India's largest animal welfare organisation, working through a nationwide network of independently registered Units: rescue, shelter and adoption, animal birth control and anti-rabies programmes, cruelty complaints and prosecution, enforcement of animal protection laws, and engagement with government on policy. The Zonal Head is PFA's designated coordinator for all recognised and proposed Units within the assigned Zone. It is a field-based, enforcement- and movement-building role: growing PFA's presence across the Zone, building and mentoring local leadership and volunteers, ensuring an effective animal welfare and enforcement response on the ground, and coordinating with police, veterinary and civic authorities. Each Unit remains independently registered and self-governing; the Zonal Head coordinates and supports them and carries directions from the Principal Organisation. The nine Zones North North : Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir North : Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh Central 1 : Uttar Pradesh Central 2 : Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh East : Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha North East : Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Sikkim West : Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Goa, Daman and Diu South : Andhra Pradesh, Telangana South South : Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka Network and leadership Map the Zone State-wise and district-wise, identify gaps in PFA presence, support new and existing Units, and identify, recommend and mentor local leadership for District and State Units. Build a pipeline of active workers so that no district is left without a first responder. Make PFA Units in each district. Coordination Coordinate with State Coordinators and District Heads, convene review meetings, resolve inter-Unit disputes, and ensure directions from the Principal Organisation are carried out. Animal welfare and enforcement response Prompt, documented action on cruelty, abandonment, injury and neglect complaints: Guide Units in registering complaints and FIRs and in invoking the strongest available provisions. Secure custody of rescued or seized animals as case property under the PCA (Care and Maintenance of Case Property Animals) Rules, 2017, and ensure their care pending trial. Maintain evidentiary discipline: dated photographs and video, witness details, veterinary certificates and a clear chain of custody, so cases survive prosecution rather than collapsing at the complaint stage. Liaise with SHOs, prosecutors, veterinary officers and Honorary Animal Welfare Officers to see cases through to chargesheet and conviction, and track outcomes. Scope of issues (illustrative, not exhaustive) Companion and street animals : cruelty to dogs and cats including poisoning and illegal killing, feeding disputes with RWAs and authorities, unlawful relocation of community animals, gaps in ABC programmes. Cattle and large animals : abandoned cattle, gaushala conditions, illegal and cruel transport, unlicensed and cruel slaughter, disease-driven distress. Working animals : equines at brick kilns, tourism sites, weddings and construction; bullocks and draught animals; camels; unfit-to-work animals; lack of water, shade or farriery. Farmed animals : battery cages, live-bird markets, piggeries, cruel handling in transport and markets. Aquatic animals : live fish and seafood transport and market handling; the ornamental fish trade. Wildlife and trade : poaching, snaring and trapping, illegal bird and exotic-pet trade (including CITES-listed species), monkey and parakeet capture, and rescues where people and wildlife share space. Captive and performing animals : captive elephants and temple animals, circuses and unregistered performing animals, roadside menageries, animal-drawn-vehicle abuse. Blood sports and rituals : cockfighting, dog and other animal fighting, bull-taming events, bullock-cart racing, cruelty in religious sacrifice. Seasonal hazards : glass-coated kite string (manja) injuries to birds, festival firecracker distress, heat-wave, cold-wave and monsoon response. Establishments : pet shops (Pet Shop Rules, 2018), dog breeders (Dog Breeding and Marketing Rules, 2017), livestock markets: registration, inspection and closure of illegal operators. Trauma and access to care : road-accident and roadkill response, and access to first aid, ambulances and veterinary treatment. Movement building and community mobilisation Expand the Rapid Response Team app district-wise and drive ABC (per the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023), anti-rabies vaccination, native and community-dog adoption, sterilisation and vaccination camps, "Be Kind to Animals" outreach and other PFA programmes against measurable district-wise targets. Recruit, train and retain a volunteer and first-responder base in every district; recognise local heroes to sustain morale. Build Animal Welfare Societies on college and school campuses, kept engaged through structured humane-education activities. Support and protect community feeders and caregivers, and mediate neighbourhood conflicts. Build local coalitions with sympathetic veterinarians, lawyers, police officers, RWAs, other NGOs and the media, so PFA's reach outlasts any single individual. Use local and social media to document work, run awareness campaigns, and grow a local supporter and donor base for Unit sustainability. Disaster and disease response Ensure Units are prepared to protect animals in floods, fires and other disasters (evacuation, feed, water, temporary shelter, veterinary aid), and to respond to disease outbreaks such as Lumpy Skin Disease and other notified diseases under the Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals Act, 2009, coordinating with district administration and veterinary authorities. Institution building Drive the nomination, appointment and coordination of Honorary Animal Welfare Officers across the Zone as a standing enforcement resource. Follow up with authorities on the constitution and functioning of SPCAs in the districts and State Animal Welfare Boards in the States of the Zone. Push for functional infrastructure (ambulances, helplines, shelters, treatment facilities) and tie-ups with veterinary colleges and hospitals. Training and reporting Ensure Units and volunteers are trained in animal welfare law, rescue and handling, evidence and PFA protocols; maintain a Zone-wide register of Units, office bearers and HAWOs; and submit a consolidated quarterly Zone Report against targets, with case and outcome data. Eligibility Preferably an active working member of a recognised PFA Unit within the Zone. Experience in animal welfare, rescue, NGO management, social work or community organising. Strong organisational, people and communication skills; willingness to travel extensively and respond at short notice. Working knowledge of animal welfare law, enforcement mechanisms and government structures is a strong advantage. Accountability The Zonal Head reports to the Chairperson / Principal Organisation and is assessed on network growth, animal welfare and enforcement response, programme delivery, government coordination, movement building, training, compliance and reporting. The Zonal Head must act in the interests of PFA, maintain confidentiality, disclose conflicts of interest, and not use the position for personal, political or commercial gain. About the role The Sanjay Gandhi Animal Care Centre is PFA's flagship in Delhi: an animal hospital and shelter in one, caring for more than three thousand animals at any one time, round the clock. It treats every kind of animal the city brings to its gate, from community dogs and cats to cattle, horses, donkeys and birds. A vet here sees in a month what many see in a year, and helps train the Indian vets and para vets who work alongside. What the work is Treat in-patients in the wards and out-patients at the gate, across many species. Surgery in the centre's operation theatre, including the animal birth control programme for the city's community dogs. Intensive care for large animals and small ones, with X-ray and blood tests on site. Teach: share what you know with the centre's vets, para vets and students. Who it suits A qualified veterinarian, for the senior and junior posts; a trained para vet for the para vet post. Students and visiting vets who want hands-on experience across species, as volunteers. Anyone who can stay calm with a frightened animal, and kind with a frightened owner. See the centre: Sanjay Gandhi Animal Care Centre . Before this goes live, download each one, confirm PFA holds the rights, and re-point the src at a self-hosted copy in /img alongside the portrait. Hot-linking another server's assets breaks the moment they rename a file, and it spends their bandwidth, not yours. Every frame falls back to a labelled placeholder if its source fails, so swapping sources can never leave a broken image on the page. Ideal sizes: portrait 1200x1600 or larger, gallery 1600x1100 or larger. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- --> Founder Maneka Sanjay Gandhi Founder and chairperson of People for Animals. She started the organisation and built it into India’s largest animal welfare body, with hospitals, shelters, mobile clinics and members in every part of the country. Compassion without action is evil Smt. Maneka Sanjay Gandhi Smt. Maneka Sanjay Gandhi Founder and chairperson, People for Animals Watch Her, in motion. Hover a frame · press play 26 Animal hospitals 90+ PFA units across the country 60 Mobile units on the road 1M+ Lives touched In her words A circle of love around all life. Her argument starts with self-interest, not sentiment. Every species, from bees to elephants, holds up a shield around human life, and the quality of our own lives rests on theirs. Eat them, exploit them, breed one kind while wiping out another, and the damage lands back on us: as each species goes, our own world gets poorer. Her invitation is simply to join the circle of care around all living things. People for Animals turned animal welfare in India from a quiet cause into an organised, assertive movement. Its members are lawyers, film actors, business leaders, civil servants, teachers and students. The work runs from shelters and ambulances through to fighting cases in court, training judges, police officers and bureaucrats, and publishing material that teaches people how to care for animals. Its wins have come in courtrooms, in research laboratories, and at racecourses, temples, circuses and zoos. PFA is now counted among the strongest animal groups anywhere in the world. When the first International Animal Welfare Directory was assembled, its British publishers asked PFA to write the foreword. In 2001 the first Padma Shri awarded in this field went to a PFA member, Dr Norma Alvares. What she set out to build. The strategy behind the organisation, and the target it still works towards: an animal welfare centre in every district in India, of which there are now about 800. 01 Create infrastructure Build and upgrade the physical means of rescue: shelters, ambulances, mobile clinics and helplines that answer when someone finds an injured animal. 02 Influence policy Work as a pressure group for legislation that protects animals and the environment, rather than waiting for it to arrive on its own. 03 Make the law bite Take direct action through PFA units nationwide, so that animals are protected in practice and offenders actually face consequences. 04 Educate and sensitise Animal welfare groups in schools and colleges, training for lawyers, police, the judiciary and civil servants, and published guides on animal care. 05 Advance the movement Work alongside Indian and international welfare groups, fund initiatives that deserve it, and open real career paths in animal welfare. 06 Change what we eat Make the health, environmental and economic case for plant-based choices, and find and promote alternatives that use no animals at all. India has drafted new rules for animals used in laboratories. Until 5 November 2026 anyone can object. Ask for independent oversight, protection for community animals, and alternatives to animal experiments, in a letter sent from your own email. Write your objection Last date 5 November 2026 What to ask for Three changes. 01 Keep oversight independent. The draft would let an institution's own ethics committee approve mild and moderate experiments. Ask for outside review and open severity assessments. 02 Close the gaps in sourcing. Its exceptions for "stray or feral" animals need scrutiny. Ask for traceable sources, and no capture of community animals. 03 Make alternatives the priority. Replacement, reduction and refinement must mean action: enforceable welfare standards, public reporting, and investment in methods without animals. pages.body: Laws | People for Animals Every drive, camp and open day is free to attend ✕ Laws Animal laws. Before you cite any of this. Every answer names the provision it rests on, so you can check it rather than take it on trust. Read the section on indiacode.nic.in before you quote it, and check your State: prevention of cruelty is a concurrent subject, so State rules and municipal by-laws sit on top of everything here. A section cited wrongly in an FIR is harder to correct than one left out. Last read against the statutes in August 2026. All Dogs Cattle Husbandry Equines Expand all Showing every question that rests on Clear Dogs A1 Which law protects dogs from cruelty? Two provisions, always read together. Section 3 of the PCA Act 1960 puts a positive duty on anyone in charge of an animal to prevent unnecessary pain, so inaction is itself actionable. Section 11(1) then lists the offences: beating, kicking, overloading, starving, confining, abandoning and more. Basis PCA 1960 s.3 PCA 1960 s.11(1) A2 Which section carries a real sentence for cruelty? Where the animal is killed, poisoned, maimed or rendered useless, BNS Section 325 carries up to five years and is a cognizable offence, so the police are obliged to register an FIR rather than take a complaint and sit on it. It applies to any animal, owned or not, and the old value thresholds in IPC 428 and 429 are gone. Charge it there. The PCA Act alone is not worth filing under: its penalty has never been raised from the 1960 figures, and the 2022 amendment that would raise it is still not enacted. Careful Section 325 is mischief, so it needs an intentional act: starving, neglect and failure to treat are not mischief, and belong under PCA Section 11 read with Section 3. And it is bailable, so expect the accused to be released; the value of the section is that it forces registration and carries a real sentence at trial, not that it holds anyone. Basis PCA 1960 s.11(1) BNS 2023 s.325 A3 Is killing or maiming a dog a crime? Yes, and it is the serious charge. BNS Section 325, which replaced IPC 428 and 429, punishes killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless any animal with up to five years, or fine, or both. Do this Insist the FIR names Section 325 and not merely the PCA Act. Basis BNS 2023 s.325 A4 Can one be jailed for poisoning community dogs? Yes. Section 11(1)(l) of the PCA Act protects street dogs by name from being poisoned with strychnine or harmed by any other unnecessarily cruel method. Add BNS Section 325 for the custodial sentence. Ask for a post mortem, because the toxicology report is the evidence the case rests on. Basis PCA 1960 s.11(1)(l) BNS 2023 s.325 A5 What are the ABC Rules 2023? Rules framed under Section 38 of the PCA Act for managing community dogs: humane capture, sterilisation and vaccination, then return of the dog to the exact place it came from. Return to its own locality is the rule, not a concession. The local body must run the programme through an AWBI recognised organisation. Basis ABC Rules 2023 PCA 1960 s.38 A6 Who is responsible for community dogs in my area? The local body, meaning your municipal corporation, city municipal council or gram panchayat. The ABC Rules 2023 place the duty to run sterilisation and anti rabies vaccination on it, not on residents or feeders. If it has no ABC programme, that is a default you can act on in writing. Basis ABC Rules 2023 A7 Can community dogs be relocated? As a rule, no. The ABC Rules require a sterilised and vaccinated dog to go back to its own locality, and relocation is not a lawful method of managing community dogs. The Supreme Court order of 19 May 2026 made a narrow exception for premises such as schools, hospitals, sports complexes, bus stands and railway stations: dogs from there are sterilised, vaccinated and given safe placement in a designated shelter, where they are to be cared for. Do this Read that as a narrow exception, not a licence, and ask that any dog placed in a shelter receives proper care there. Careful This is a continuing suo motu matter now monitored by every High Court, so check the current position before relying on it. Basis ABC Rules 2023 SC 19 May 2026 A8 What did the Supreme Court's May 2026 judgment say? That the ABC Rules remain the framework for humane management of community dogs, through sterilisation and vaccination; that dogs from schools, hospitals and similar premises are to be sterilised, vaccinated and given safe placement in a designated shelter; that every district must have at least one working ABC centre; and that officials who do not follow the directions are answerable. It also upheld the AWBI’s standard operating procedure, which is the document a municipality works from. The mandatory district centre is the part most useful to citizens and to the animals. Careful The proceedings continue and High Courts are monitoring compliance, so directions can move. Basis SC 19 May 2026 ABC Rules 2023 A9 When may a community dog be humanely euthanised? Only on three grounds under the 2026 directions, each to be assessed by qualified veterinary experts: rabies, an incurable illness causing suffering, or severe aggression established on evidence. A resident complaint is not a ground. It must be done humanely by a registered veterinarian. Anything else is an offence under BNS Section 325. Careful The judgment says “rabid”, not “laboratory confirmed”, and the safeguard it names is assessment by qualified veterinary experts. Ask for that assessment on record rather than for a lab report the order does not require. Basis SC 19 May 2026 PCA 1960 s.13 BNS 2023 s.325 A10 Is feeding community dogs legal? Yes, and obstructing a feeder is the actionable conduct, not the feeding. The ABC Rules 2023 require resident associations and local bodies to designate feeding spots. The Delhi High Court in Dr Maya D. Chablani v. Radha Mittal (2021) held that community dogs have a right to food and that citizens have a right to feed them, subject to using designated points and keeping them clean. Basis ABC Rules 2023 r.20 Chablani (Del HC 2021) Art 51A(g) A11 Can my apartment RWA ban pets or the feeding of community animals? No. A resident association is a private body and cannot override rules made under a central Act. AWBI guidelines and repeated High Court rulings hold that an RWA cannot ban pets, bar them from lifts, or prohibit feeding. It may regulate reasonably, meaning time and place, and nothing more. Careful The May 2026 judgment read “gated campus” in the ABC Rules narrowly, so a society enclosing a school, hospital or similar premises may stand differently from an ordinary residential block. Basis ABC Rules 2023 AWBI guidelines Chablani (Del HC 2021) A12 Can a housing society fine me for my dog barking? It can ask for reasonable steps. Barking is not a ground for sending the animal away, and AWBI guidance says so directly. A resolution passed by a majority does not become lawful merely because it was passed. Basis AWBI guidelines A13 Do I need a dog licence? It depends on your local body, since this is a municipal by-law subject and not a central one. Many corporations require annual registration of pet dogs. Check Udupi City Municipal Council for the local position. Registration is also the quickest way to bring your dog home if it is ever lost or taken in by the municipality. Basis Municipal by-laws A14 Is rabies vaccination compulsory? In practice, yes. Rabies is notifiable under the PCICDA 2009, and annual anti rabies vaccination is required for municipal registration, for travel, and for the National Action Plan for Dog Mediated Rabies Elimination by 2030. Do this Keep the certificate, since it is what protects you if a bite is alleged. Basis PCICDA 2009 NAPRE 2030 A15 Are Pitbulls and Rottweilers banned in India? No valid nationwide ban exists. A central letter of March 2024 asked States to prohibit 23 breeds. Within weeks six High Courts had set it aside or stayed it, two quashing it outright, for want of consultation with the people it affected and for treating breed as a proxy for danger. Do this Check your own municipality, but a mere advisory is not law. Basis Central advisory 2024 Kar HC 2024 A16 Do dog breeders need a licence? Yes. The Dog Breeding and Marketing Rules 2017 require registration with the State Animal Welfare Board, minimum housing and veterinary standards, and record keeping. A female may not be bred below 18 months or more than once a year. An unregistered breeder is operating illegally, and photographs of the premises are worth more than a complaint. Basis Dog Breeding and Marketing Rules 2017 A17 Do pet shops need a licence? Yes. The Pet Shop Rules 2018 require registration with the State Animal Welfare Board, space and veterinary norms, and prohibit the sale of animals under eight weeks old. Selling from an unregistered shop is an offence under the parent PCA Act. Basis Pet Shop Rules 2018 PCA 1960 s.38 A18 Can one buy a puppy online or on the roadside? Sale by an unregistered breeder or seller violates the 2017 and 2018 Rules. The buyer is not usually prosecuted, but has almost no remedy when the animal turns out to be sick or underage, and buying sustains the trade the Rules exist to stop. The useful step is the other way round: report the seller to the State Animal Welfare Board, which is the authority those Rules make responsible for registration, with the listing, the address and any photographs. Where animals are kept in conditions that cause suffering, that is also Section 11 of the PCA Act. Basis Dog Breeding and Marketing Rules 2017 Pet Shop Rules 2018 A19 Is ear cropping or tail docking legal? Treat it as mutilation. Section 11(1)(l) of the PCA Act prohibits mutilating an animal, and cosmetic cropping or docking has no medical justification. The AWBI circular of 2011 and Veterinary Council ethics treat it as professional misconduct, so the veterinarian who performs it can be proceeded against. Basis PCA 1960 s.11(1)(l) AWBI circular 2011 VCI ethics A20 Are dog fights legal? No. Section 11(1)(m) covers organising, keeping or using premises for animal fighting, and Section 11(1)(n) covers promoting a fight or merely being present at one. Spectators are liable. Where a dog dies, add BNS Section 325. Basis PCA 1960 s.11(1)(m) PCA 1960 s.11(1)(n) BNS 2023 s.325 A21 Can one abandon a dog? No. Section 11(1)(i) makes it an offence to abandon an animal in circumstances likely to cause it suffering from starvation or thirst. If the animal dies, the abandonment becomes a killing and BNS Section 325 applies. Surrender to a shelter instead, which is lawful. Basis PCA 1960 s.11(1)(i) BNS 2023 s.325 A22 Can one keep a dog chained all day? No. Section 11(1)(f) specifically prohibits keeping an animal chained on an unreasonably short or heavy chain for an unreasonable period. Do this Read with the Section 3 duty of care, prolonged tethering is cruelty on its face and photographs establish it. Basis PCA 1960 s.11(1)(f) PCA 1960 s.3 A23 What are the rules for transporting dogs? The Transport of Animals Rules 1978 prescribe crate size, ventilation, water and a veterinary fitness certificate for rail and air. Independently, Section 11(1)(d) of the PCA Act makes conveying an animal in a way that causes unnecessary pain an offence, so a breach of the Rules and a cruelty offence usually arise on the same facts. Basis Transport of Animals Rules 1978 PCA 1960 s.11(1)(d) A24 Can I take my dog on a train? Yes. Indian Railways permits dogs in a first class AC coupe or first class cabin on booking, or in the brake van dog box. Carry the vaccination certificate. Confining an animal in the brake van without water or ventilation remains cruelty regardless of the ticket. Basis Transport of Animals Rules 1978 PCA 1960 s.11(1)(d) A25 Can I fly with my dog in India? Yes, in cabin or cargo depending on the airline, with health and vaccination certificates. Each carrier sets its own crate and weight conditions under DGCA guid

pages.body: Privacy policy | People for Animals Every drive, camp and open day is free to attend ✕ Privacy policy Privacy, in plain words. What this website keeps, why, and how to ask for it back. Make a request The full policy The short version No tracking No advertising cookies, no analytics that follow you, no third-party trackers. Only what you send The site keeps what you type into a form, and the few things needed to act on it. Never sold Your details are not sold, rented or traded, to anyone, ever. Yours to ask for A copy, a correction or erasure, under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Last updated 9 October 2026 The policy Open what you need. Who we are People for Animals (PFA) is a registered charitable trust, founded by Smt. Maneka Sanjay Gandhi, with its registered office at 4-T, DCM Building, 16 Barakhamba Road, New Delhi 110001. For this website, PFA decides what is collected and why, so under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 it is the Data Fiduciary for what you send here. What we collect Only what you give, when you choose to give it: Forms. Reporting cruelty, asking a question, volunteering, applying for a job, a membership, a colony caregiver card, an event, a campus society, a campaign, a partnership, a legacy enquiry or a request on this page. Each takes your name, a way to reach you (email, mobile or both) and what you write. Photographs. Up to three with a cruelty report, and your own photograph with a caregiver card application, for the card. Please leave out faces and number plates unless they matter to the report. Payments. For a donation, membership, card fee or shop order: the amount, what it is for, your name, contact details and, where needed, a postal address. A PAN, only if you give one for an 80G receipt. Card and bank details go to the payment provider, never to PFA. A gift. If you give in someone's name: their name and where to send the certificate. Replies. If you answer an email from PFA, your reply is filed with your submission, so the whole conversation is in one place. A location, if you ask. Pressing "use my location" sends your position once, to fill in the address. It is not tracked. What we do not collect No advertising or analytics cookies, and no tracking pixels. The website sets no cookies of its own. No record of what you type into search. The site counts which pages people open from search, as a number against the page, and nothing about who opened them. No profile of you built from your visits. The visit counter in the footer is a single number. Your network address is used for up to an hour to stop floods of automated submissions, and is stored only as a one-way scramble that cannot be turned back into the address. Why we use it To act on what you sent: pass a report to the right people, answer a question, consider an application, issue a card, a certificate or a receipt. To reply to you, and to send the confirmation with your reference number. To keep a true record of PFA's work, and of the money it receives, as the law asks of a charity. To keep the site safe from abuse. PFA relies on your consent, given when you send a form, and on the uses the law allows without it, such as keeping financial records or helping in an emergency. PFA does not send newsletters or appeals you did not ask for. Who else handles it Every submission is copied to PFA's office inbox. Beyond PFA, a few providers handle data, each only for its own part: Google Cloud (Firebase) stores the submissions, photographs and the admin panel's records. Vercel and Google Firebase host the website and the server that receives forms. CCAvenue takes payments in India; your card or bank details stay with them. PayPal takes gifts from outside India, and issues its own receipt. PFA's mailbox, with a backup sender, sends confirmations, replies and the office copy of each submission. OpenStreetMap, BigDataCloud and India Post turn a location or a pincode into an address, only when you ask. YouTube and Vimeo play the films; YouTube in its privacy-enhanced mode. Authorities , when the law requires it, or to act on a cruelty report. Films sent to The Wall, and nominations to CineKind, may be shown publicly, as the form says before you send. Nothing else you send is published. Where it is kept, and how it is protected Submissions are read only by PFA staff signed in to the admin panel. Every change a staff member makes is written to an audit log. Photographs and documents are kept in private storage that no browser can open; staff see them only through the signed-in admin panel. Following a submission on the site needs both its reference number and the email or mobile it was sent with. Connections to the site are encrypted. Some providers above may process data on servers outside India; PFA uses only providers bound to keep it secure. How long it is kept A submission is kept as PFA's record of the work, until you ask for it to be erased. Payment and donation records are kept for as long as tax and charity law require, even if you ask otherwise. A photograph uploaded for a caregiver card that is never paid for is deleted after a day. The scrambles used against floods expire after an hour at most. What your browser keeps A few conveniences are saved in your own browser's storage, not on PFA's servers, and never sent anywhere: your shopping bag, your recent searches, the reference numbers you have followed, your reading place and settings in the library, your choices on The Wall and in the cinema player, and a half-filled caregiver application so it is not lost. Clearing your browser's site data removes them all. Children The forms are meant for adults. Anyone under 18 should ask a parent or guardian to send a form with them, or for them. If PFA learns it holds a child's details without that, it will erase them, except where they are needed to help an animal in danger. Your rights Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you may ask PFA: For a summary of what PFA holds about you, and who it was shared with. To correct it , complete it, or bring it up to date. To erase it , unless the law requires PFA to keep it. To stop : withdraw your consent. What was done before stays lawful. To hear a grievance , and to escalate it to the Data Protection Board of India. To nominate someone to act for you if you die or cannot act yourself. Make a request . PFA may confirm it is you first, and replies within the time the law sets. Changes to this policy When the site changes what it collects or why, this page changes first, with a new date at the top. A change that needs your consent again will ask for it. Contact and grievances People for Animals, 4-T, DCM Building, 16 Barakhamba Road, New Delhi 110001. pages.title: Someone, not something | People for Animals
pages.description: What the science says about the animals we eat: memory, self-control, play and feeling in hens, pigs, cows and goats, with every claim sourced.
headings: The pig who played video games
What they know, learn and remember
What they feel, and how we can tell
pages.body: Someone, not something | People for Animals Every drive, camp and open day is free to attend ✕ What animal welfare is. Sources What the science says about the animals we eat. Eight short chapters: memory, self-control, play and feeling, with a quiz at the end and the sources beneath it. Not a flock. Individuals. A hen keeps track of the faces of many individual flockmates, holds a stable place in a pecking order, and uses more than twenty distinct calls. In one study, hens chose to wait for a larger food reward rather than take a smaller one immediately, a form of self-control. She is someone, not something. See the evidence Face memory Recognition Hens recognise and remember individual flockmates, and hold a stable place in a pecking order that depends on knowing exactly who is who. A patient bird Self-control Given the choice, hens have opted to wait several seconds longer for a larger portion of food instead of taking a smaller one straight away. Mirror test Problem-solving Pigs shown food only as a reflection worked out where it really was: seven of eight walked straight to the hidden bowl rather than behind the mirror. Nest builders Motherhood Given straw and room, a sow spends the day before giving birth building a nest, a behaviour that has survived thousands of years of domestication. The pig who played video games In a 2021 study, four pigs learned to move a cursor with a joystick and hit on-screen targets, well above chance, using only their snouts. Pigs also use mirrors to find hidden food, and their grunts carry information about how they feel: software trained on thousands of recorded calls could tell positive from negative states with over 90% accuracy. Test yourself What they know, learn and remember Sources Cows Learning Heifers that worked out how to press a panel to open a gate showed rising heart rates and livelier movement than controls, a response researchers read as excitement at solving the task. Goats Memory Goats mastered a two-step puzzle box and still solved it ten months later. When a task becomes impossible, they turn to look at a nearby human, much as dogs do. Sheep Faces Sheep can learn the faces of about fifty other sheep and remember them for up to two years. They can also pick out familiar human faces from photographs. Horses Reading us Shown photographs of angry human faces, horses' heart rates rose and they looked with the left eye, the side linked to processing threats. Happy faces drew no such reaction. What they feel, and how we can tell Sources Play Positive welfare Calves, lambs and kids play more when well fed and unstressed, and play drops when conditions worsen. Researchers treat it as a sign an animal is doing well, not just surviving. Optimism Judgement bias Like people, animals in a poor state read ambiguous cues pessimistically. Calves tested after hot-iron disbudding were less likely to approach an uncertain cue, a measurable sign of a negative mood. Company Social bonds Isolated sheep show stress in behaviour, hormones and brain activity, and pictures of sheep faces alone reduce it. Horses groomed at the withers, where they groom each other, show lowered heart rates. Ear talk Body language Cows' ears hint at mood: gently stroked, they settle their ears into more relaxed positions. Goats, for their part, prefer looking at photographs of smiling human faces over angry ones. Things science did not expect → → Chicks a few days old watched small groups of objects move behind two screens, then reliably went to the screen hiding the larger number. They were tracking additions and subtractions of quantities up to five. Rugani and colleagues, 2009 When their chicks received a harmless puff of air, mother hens' heart rates rose, their eye temperature dropped, and they stood alert and called to the chicks. Their own bodies responded to their chicks' mild distress. Edgar and colleagues, 2011 Horses shown a photograph of a person with an angry expression later behaved more warily toward that same person, met in real life hours afterwards with a neutral face. They had remembered the emotion and attached it to the individual. Proops and colleagues, 2018 Current Biology Goats learned a two-step puzzle box, pulling a lever and then lifting it to release food. Ten months later, with no practice in between, most solved it again within about a minute. Briefer and colleagues, 2014 Frontiers in Zoology Who would you underestimate? Which of these animals can remember fifty faces for two years? Which one shows signs of excitement when it works out how to open a gate? Take the two-minute quiz and find out how much you already knew. Take the quiz Where this comes from Every claim on this page is drawn from peer-reviewed research in animal cognition and welfare science. Where the evidence is limited or debated, we say so. In 2014 the Supreme Court of India read the right to life in Article 21 to cover animals too, holding that they are entitled to live with intrinsic worth, honour and dignity. The same judgment brought the five freedoms into Indian law, alongside the duty of compassion for living creatures in Article 51A(g). Read the sources

The aim is an animal welfare centre in every district in India. There are about 800, and the number moves as states draw new ones and merge others. A unit begins with six board members, a bank account and one campaign, and the first priority is always the animal in front of you rather than the poster about it. rows.d: There is no dedicated chapter in the Transport of Animals Rules for fish. Transport that causes avoidable suffering can still be pressed under Section 11(1)(d), and food safety conditions apply under the FSSA 2006. Basis

rows.t: Are ornamental fish and aquarium trade regulated?
rows.p: Laws › Are ornamental fish and aquarium trade regulated?
rows.d: Import of ornamental species is controlled under the DGFT policy and quarantine requirements, and species listed under the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 cannot be traded at all. Check the schedules before buying anythin

rows.t: What is the PCICDA 2009?
rows.p: Laws › What is the PCICDA 2009?
rows.d: The Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals Act 2009. It makes listed diseases notifiable, obliges the person in charge of an animal to report them, and empowers the government to declare

rows.t: Which animal diseases are notifiable?
rows.p: Laws › Which animal diseases are notifiable?
rows.d: Those listed in the Schedule to the PCICDA 2009, which includes foot and mouth disease, anthrax, brucellosis, rabies, avian influenza and others. The Schedule is amended from time to time, so check the current notificati

rows.t: What happens during an avian influenza outbreak?
rows.p: Laws › What happens during an avian influenza outbreak?
rows.d: The government declares an infected zone, restricts movement and orders culling and disposal under the PCICDA 2009 and the departmental action plan. Culling must still be carried out by methods that avoid unnecessary suf

rows.t: Is compensation payable for culled poultry?
rows.p: Laws › Is compensation payable for culled poultry?
rows.d: Yes, at rates fixed by the central and State action plans for the disease concerned. Claims are made through the animal husbandry department, and rates change, so rely on the current notification rather than a published

rows.t: Are antibiotics in animal feed regulated?
rows.p: Laws › Are antibiotics in animal feed regulated?
rows.d: Yes. The FSSA framework prescribes maximum residue limits in food of animal origin, and the use of antibiotics as growth promoters has been restricted by notification. Residue testing is the enforcement tool, and it sits

rows.t: Is hormone use in dairy or poultry legal?
rows.p: Laws › Is hormone use in dairy or poultry legal?
rows.d: Oxytocin for milk letdown is prohibited and its sale is restricted. Administering an injurious substance to an animal is an offence under Section 11(1)(c) and Section 12 of the PCA Act, quite apart from food safety conse

rows.t: Do animal farms need environmental clearance?
rows.p: Laws › Do animal farms need environmental clearance?
rows.d: Large units require consent to establish and consent to operate from the State pollution control board, and effluent and waste disposal are regulated. A farm operating without consent can be directed to close, which is o

rows.t: Can a farm be shut for cruelty?
rows.p: Laws › Can a farm be shut for cruelty?
rows.d: The PCA Act does not provide a closure power by itself, but the licensing authority, the food safety authority and the pollution control board each can. A cruelty complaint filed alongside a licensing complaint is far mo

rows.t: Are there rules for animal markets?
rows.p: Laws › Are there rules for animal markets?
rows.d: Markets are regulated by State market committee law and municipal by-laws, with animal health conditions under the PCICDA 2009. The central Livestock Market Rules 2017 were stayed and withdrawn, so do not rely on them. B

rows.t: Can animals be sold at a market without health certification?
rows.p: Laws › Can animals be sold at a market without health certification
rows.d: Movement and sale of animals from a controlled area without certification breaches the PCICDA 2009. Separately, offering for sale an animal that is diseased or suffering is an offence under Section 11(1)(k). Basis PCICDA

rows.t: Is animal experimentation regulated?
rows.p: Laws › Is animal experimentation regulated?
rows.d: Yes. Section 15 of the PCA Act constitutes the Committee for the Purpose of Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals, and the Breeding of and Experiments on Animals Rules 1998 govern institutional ethics committ

rows.t: Is cosmetics testing on animals banned in India?
rows.p: Laws › Is cosmetics testing on animals banned in India?
rows.d: Yes. The Drugs and Cosmetics Rules were amended to prohibit testing of cosmetics on animals and to prohibit the import of cosmetics tested on animals. India was among the first countries in Asia to do this. Basis Drugs a

rows.t: Can students dissect animals in school?
rows.p: Laws › Can students dissect animals in school?
rows.d: Dissection has been phased out in school curricula and restricted in undergraduate courses by UGC and MCI directions, with alternatives prescribed. Institutional use of animals otherwise requires CPCSEA registration. Bas

rows.t: Are circuses allowed to use animals?
rows.p: Laws › Are circuses allowed to use animals?

rows.t: Are elephants allowed in temples and processions?
rows.p: Laws › Are elephants allowed in temples and processions?
rows.d: Captive elephants require ownership certificates under the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 and must comply with AWBI and Project Elephant guidelines on chaining, work hours and transport. Courts have repeatedly restrained

rows.t: Can wild animals be kept as pets?
rows.p: Laws › Can wild animals be kept as pets?
rows.d: No. Possession of a scheduled wild animal without authority is an offence under the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972, punishable with imprisonment. This includes many birds, tortoises and reptiles sold openly in markets. B

rows.t: Is keeping Indian birds in cages legal?
rows.p: Laws › Is keeping Indian birds in cages legal?

rows.t: What is the penalty under the Wildlife Act?
rows.p: Laws › What is the penalty under the Wildlife Act?

rows.t: Who enforces the Wildlife Act?
rows.p: Laws › Who enforces the Wildlife Act?
rows.d: The forest department, through the Chief Wildlife Warden and authorised officers, with police assistance. Wildlife offences are cognizable and non bailable for the higher schedules, and seized animals become government p

rows.t: Can I keep bees or is apiculture regulated?
rows.p: Laws › Can I keep bees or is apiculture regulated?

rows.t: Are working bullocks in agriculture protected?
rows.p: Laws › Are working bullocks in agriculture protected?
rows.d: Yes, by Section 11(1)(a) and Section 11(1)(b), which cover overloading, beating and employing an unfit animal. State bullock cart rules also prescribe load limits in some places. Basis PCA 1960 s.11(1)(a) PCA 1960 s.11(1

rows.t: Is there a legal duty to provide shade and water?
rows.p: Laws › Is there a legal duty to provide shade and water?
rows.d: Yes, through Section 3, which requires the person in charge to take reasonable measures for the wellbeing of the animal, and through Section 11(1)(h) on failure to provide food and water. Denial of water in the Indian su

rows.t: Can I complain about a neighbour's neglected livestock?
rows.p: Laws › Can I complain about a neighbour's neglected livestock?

rows.t: What is an Honorary Animal Welfare Officer?
rows.p: Laws › What is an Honorary Animal Welfare Officer?
rows.d: A person appointed by the AWBI who can visit premises, assist the police at a seizure and report violations. The appointment carries no police power, but it gives standing and it usually gets the door opened. Basis PCA 1

rows.t: Can an FIR be filed against a company or a farm owner?
rows.p: Laws › Can an FIR be filed against a company or a farm owner?
rows.d: Yes. Where the offence is by a company, the persons in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business can be proceeded against. Name the proprietor or the responsible manager, not just the estab

rows.p: Laws › Is animal fat or by-product processing regulated?

rows.p: Laws › Are leather tanneries connected to animal law?
rows.d: The welfare offences arise upstream, in transport and slaughter, and are prosecuted under the PCA Act and the State cattle preservation law. Tannery operation itself is governed by pollution control law. Basis PCA 1960 s

rows.t: Can I object to an animal sacrifice at a local festival?
rows.p: Laws › Can I object to an animal sacrifice at a local festival?
rows.d: Yes. Several States prohibit sacrifice by specific legislation, and where that applies the local police can act. Where it does not, the transport and confinement of the animal beforehand remain prosecutable under Section

rows.t: Are there subsidies tied to welfare compliance?
rows.p: Laws › Are there subsidies tied to welfare compliance?

rows.p: Laws › Who regulates veterinary practice?
rows.d: The Veterinary Council of India under the Indian Veterinary Council Act 1984, with State veterinary councils registering practitioners. Professional misconduct, including performing cosmetic mutilation, is a disciplinary

rows.t: Can a vet refuse to treat an injured street animal?
rows.p: Laws › Can a vet refuse to treat an injured street animal?
rows.d: There is no statutory duty to treat, but veterinary ethics require humane handling and first aid in an emergency, and a government veterinary hospital is expected to attend to an animal brought in. Refusal can be raised

rows.p: Laws › Is horse riding on the beach regulated?
rows.d: Yes, through district administration permission and Coastal Regulation Zone conditions, with local bodies restricting hours and rider loads. Welfare complaints still go under the PCA Act and the 1965 Rules. Basis CRZ Not

rows.p: Laws › Are joyride ponies at hill stations regulated?

rows.t: What is glanders and why does it matter?
rows.p: Laws › What is glanders and why does it matter?
rows.d: A notifiable equine disease under the PCICDA 2009. On confirmation the government can restrict movement, order testing, and direct culling of positive animals, with compensation payable at notified rates. Basis PCICDA 20

rows.t: Is compensation payable when a horse is culled for glanders?
rows.p: Laws › Is compensation payable when a horse is culled for glanders?
rows.d: Yes, at rates notified by the department, historically lower for mules and donkeys than for horses. Rates are revised, so confirm the current departmental rate rather than relying on an older figure. Basis PCICDA 2009 D1

rows.t: Can horse movement be restricted during an outbreak?
rows.p: Laws › Can horse movement be restricted during an outbreak?
rows.d: Yes. Under the PCICDA 2009 the government may declare a controlled area and prohibit movement of equines into or out of it. Moving an animal in breach is an offence and spreads the outbreak. Basis PCICDA 2009 D14 Are hor

rows.t: Are horse races legal?
rows.p: Laws › Are horse races legal?

rows.t: Is whipping a racehorse an offence?
rows.p: Laws › Is whipping a racehorse an offence?
rows.d: Beating an animal so as to cause unnecessary pain is an offence under Section 11(1)(a). Racing rules cap whip use, and a breach of those rules is evidence that the pain caused was unnecessary rather than incidental. Basi

rows.t: Can horses be doped for performance?
rows.p: Laws › Can horses be doped for performance?

rows.p: Laws › Are horse fights or animal fights legal?

rows.p: Laws › Can horses perform in circuses or films?

rows.p: Laws › Is the donkey hide trade regulated?
rows.d: Slaughter for hide has no lawful licence route, so the trade operates outside the FSSA framework entirely. Prosecute it as killing under BNS Section 325 with the PCA Act, and pursue transport violations alongside. Basis

rows.t: Are donkeys used in brick kilns protected?
rows.p: Laws › Are donkeys used in brick kilns protected?
rows.d: Yes, by Section 11(1)(a) and Section 11(1)(b) and by the Draught and Pack Animals Rules 1965 on load and rest. Kiln work also raises labour and pollution issues, and a joint complaint to the labour department and the pol

rows.p: Laws › Can a mule be made to carry construction material up a hill?
rows.d: Only within the load limits in the 1965 Rules, with rest and water. Loads that cause the animal to stumble or to bleed at the withers are an offence under Section 11(1)(a) read with those Rules. Basis Draught and Pack An

rows.t: Is hobbling or tight tethering of equines an offence?
rows.p: Laws › Is hobbling or tight tethering of equines an offence?
rows.d: Keeping an animal chained or tethered on an unreasonably short or heavy chain for an unreasonable period is an offence under Section 11(1)(f). Hobbling that causes injury also engages Section 11(1)(a). Basis PCA 1960 s.1

rows.p: Laws › What if a horse is abandoned when it stops working?

rows.d: There is no fixed statutory schedule, but the Section 3 duty of care covers routine health, and a working animal with untreated dental disease loses condition and becomes unfit within Section 11(1)(b). Basis PCA 1960 s.3
